1. Purpose

This policy establishes the framework under which [Company Name] ("the Company") permits employees to work remotely. It is intended to:

  1. support flexibility and work-life balance while maintaining productivity, service quality, and collaboration;
  2. protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Company information and systems wherever work is performed; and
  3. ensure remote work is applied consistently, fairly, and in compliance with applicable employment, health and safety, tax, and data protection laws.

2. Scope

2.1 This policy applies to all employees of the Company, including full-time, part-time, and fixed-term employees, who perform some or all of their work away from a Company workplace.

2.2 It also applies, as far as relevant, to contractors, interns, and temporary workers who are given access to Company systems or information, subject to the terms of their agreements.

2.3 This policy does not apply to:

  1. ordinary business travel, client-site work, or field work that is a normal requirement of the role; or
  2. work performed outside the employee's country of employment, which requires separate written approval under Section 5.6.

3. Definitions

In this policy, the following terms have the meanings set out below:

  • Remote Work – performing assigned duties from a location other than a Company workplace, typically the employee's home.
  • Fully Remote – an arrangement in which the employee's regular work is performed remotely, with only occasional on-site attendance.
  • Hybrid – an arrangement combining scheduled on-site days and remote days.
  • Remote Work Agreement – the written arrangement, approved by the employee's Manager and HR, that records the employee's work location, schedule, and conditions.
  • Remote Workspace – the designated, safe, and suitable area from which the employee performs remote work.
  • Core Hours – the hours, set by each department, during which employees must be available for meetings and communication.
  • Company Equipment – hardware, software, and accessories owned, leased, or provided by the Company.
  • Confidential Information – any non-public Company, client, or employee information, including personal data, trade secrets, financial data, and intellectual property.
  • Manager – the employee's direct line manager or supervisor.

4. Eligibility

4.1 Remote work is a privilege granted at the Company's discretion and is not a contractual entitlement. An employee may be considered for remote work if all of the following apply:

  1. the employee has completed their probationary period (normally [3] months), unless HR approves an exception;
  2. the employee's role can be performed effectively off-site without reducing service levels, security, or team collaboration;
  3. the employee's most recent performance rating is "meets expectations" or higher, and no active disciplinary action is in place;
  4. the employee has a Remote Workspace that meets the requirements of Sections 6 and 7, including a reliable internet connection; and
  5. the employee has completed required security and data protection training.

4.2 Roles that require physical presence (for example, reception, facilities, on-site equipment operation, or in-person customer service) are generally not eligible, although partial flexibility may be offered where practicable.

4.3 Eligibility decisions must be based on role requirements and business need, and must be applied consistently and without discrimination.

4.4 Employees who require remote work as a reasonable adjustment for a disability or medical condition should contact HR, and requests will be handled under the Company's accommodation procedures rather than this section.

5. Policy Provisions

  1. Approval and Remote Work Agreement
    1. Employees must submit a written request to their Manager, who will review it with HR.
    2. No remote work may begin until a Remote Work Agreement has been signed by the employee, Manager, and HR.
    3. The agreement must state:
      1. the arrangement type (Fully Remote or Hybrid) and the scheduled remote days;
      2. the address of the primary Remote Workspace; and
      3. any role-specific conditions or review dates.
    4. Arrangements are reviewed at least annually and may be modified or withdrawn as set out in Section 5.7.
  2. Working Hours and Availability
    1. Remote employees remain subject to the same terms of employment, contracted hours, and performance standards as on-site employees.
    2. Employees must be available during their department's Core Hours and respond to messages and calls within a reasonable time.
    3. Employees must:
      1. keep their calendar and status accurate and up to date;
      2. notify their Manager promptly of any unplanned absence or interruption; and
      3. record time worked accurately where timekeeping is required.
    4. Overtime must be approved in advance by the Manager, and employees must take rest breaks and leave as required by law and Company policy.
  3. Performance and Communication
    1. Performance is measured by results, quality, and conduct, not by physical presence.
    2. Managers will set clear goals, deadlines, and expectations, and hold regular check-ins at least [weekly].
    3. Employees must attend scheduled meetings, with cameras on where reasonably required, and must attend on-site meetings, training, or events when given [five] working days' notice, except in emergencies.
  4. Workspace, Health and Safety
    1. The Company remains responsible for employee health and safety while working remotely, to the extent required by law.
    2. Employees must maintain a Remote Workspace that is:
      1. safe, ergonomic, adequately lit, and free of hazards;
      2. quiet and private enough to perform work and protect Confidential Information; and
      3. suitable for work calls and video meetings.
    3. Employees must complete a workspace self-assessment on request and when they relocate.
    4. Any work-related injury or illness occurring while working remotely must be reported to the Manager and HR within 24 hours.
    5. The Company may inspect a Remote Workspace only with reasonable advance notice and the employee's consent.
  5. Expenses and Allowances
    1. The Company will reimburse reasonable, pre-approved business expenses incurred in remote work, such as required equipment, business calls, or supplies, on submission of receipts.
    2. Unless otherwise agreed in writing or required by law, the Company does not pay for:
      1. home utilities, rent, or general internet service; or
      2. furniture or home modifications beyond any approved ergonomic allowance.
    3. Remote work may have tax implications for the employee, and employees are encouraged to seek independent advice.
  6. Work Location and Relocation
    1. Employees must work from the approved location stated in their Remote Work Agreement.
    2. Employees must obtain written approval from their Manager and HR before:
      1. changing their primary work address;
      2. working from another state, province, or region; or
      3. working from another country, which may raise immigration, tax, social security, legal, and data transfer issues.
    3. Work from public places (cafés, airports, shared transport) is permitted only where Section 7 can be fully met, and Confidential Information must not be viewed or discussed there.
  7. Modification, Suspension, and Termination of Arrangements
    1. The Company may modify, suspend, or end a remote work arrangement with reasonable notice (normally [30] days) because of:
      1. changes in business needs, role, or operations;
      2. performance or conduct concerns; or
      3. a breach of this policy or the Remote Work Agreement.
    2. Where there is an urgent security, legal, or safety concern, the arrangement may be suspended immediately.
    3. An employee may request to end their arrangement by giving their Manager [30] days' written notice.
    4. Remote work does not change the employee's employment terms, benefits, or position, unless agreed in writing.

6. Equipment Requirements

6.1 Company Equipment. The Company will determine what equipment is necessary for each remote role and may provide:

  1. a laptop or other computing device with approved, managed software;
  2. a headset, webcam, and other peripherals where needed; and
  3. any other items listed in the Remote Work Agreement.

6.2 Ownership and use.

  1. Company Equipment remains the property of the Company and must be used only for authorized business purposes, with incidental personal use permitted only as allowed by the Acceptable Use Policy.
  2. Equipment must not be shared with, or used by, family members, friends, or any other person.
  3. Employees must not modify, disable, or remove Company-installed software, security controls, or settings, or install unapproved software.

6.3 Employee-provided items. Employees are responsible for providing:

  1. a reliable broadband internet connection that meets the minimum speed set by IT (currently [25 Mbps down / 5 Mbps up]);
  2. a suitable desk, chair, and lighting, unless an allowance is approved; and
  3. a secure, password-protected home Wi-Fi network using WPA2 or stronger encryption.

6.4 Personal devices (BYOD). Personal devices may be used to access Company systems only if approved by IT, enrolled in device management where required, and compliant with Section 7.

6.5 Loss, damage, and return.

  1. Lost, stolen, or damaged equipment must be reported to IT and the Manager immediately and no later than [24 hours] after discovery.
  2. Employees must take reasonable care of Company Equipment and may be held responsible for loss or damage caused by negligence, to the extent permitted by law.
  3. All Company Equipment must be returned, in good condition and within [five] working days, upon request, on termination of the remote work arrangement, or on termination of employment.

6.6 Technical support. IT will provide remote support for Company Equipment. Employees must report technical problems promptly and, if unable to work because of a problem, inform their Manager and may be asked to work from a Company workplace until it is resolved.

7. Security and Confidentiality Requirements

7.1 General obligation. Employees must comply with the Information Security Policy, Data Protection Policy, and Acceptable Use Policy at all times when working remotely.

7.2 Access and authentication.

  1. Employees must connect to Company systems only through approved methods, including the Company VPN or zero-trust access where required.
  2. Multi-factor authentication must be enabled on all Company accounts.
  3. Passwords must be strong and unique, stored only in an approved password manager, and never shared.
  4. Devices must be locked whenever unattended, and must auto-lock after no more than [five] minutes of inactivity.

7.3 Device and network security.

  1. Full-disk encryption, endpoint protection, and a host firewall must remain enabled on every device used for work.
  2. Operating systems and applications must be kept up to date, and security patches must be installed promptly when prompted by IT.
  3. Default router passwords must be changed, and public or untrusted Wi-Fi must not be used without the VPN.

7.4 Handling Confidential Information.

  1. Confidential Information must be stored only on approved Company systems and must not be saved to personal devices, personal email, or personal cloud storage.
  2. Employees must not print Confidential Information at home unless authorized. Where printing is authorized, documents must be stored securely and shredded when no longer needed.
  3. Work calls and video meetings must be held where they cannot be overheard or seen by others, and smart speakers or voice assistants should be muted or removed from the workspace during confidential discussions.
  4. Screens must be positioned, or privacy filters used, to prevent viewing by unauthorized persons.

7.5 Approved tools. Only Company-approved communication, collaboration, and storage tools may be used for work. Employees must not use unapproved applications, including personal messaging or file-sharing services, for Company business.

7.6 Incident reporting. Employees must immediately, and in any event within [one hour] of discovery, report to IT Security any actual or suspected:

  1. loss or theft of a device, or of documents containing Confidential Information;
  2. unauthorized access, phishing attempt that was acted upon, or malware infection; and
  3. disclosure of Confidential Information to an unauthorized person.

7.7 Monitoring. The Company may monitor the use of Company Equipment and systems for security and compliance purposes, in accordance with applicable law and the Company's Privacy Notice. Employees should have no expectation of privacy in Company systems.

8. Responsibilities

The following table summarizes the principal responsibilities under this policy.

RoleResponsibilities
Employee
  • Comply with this policy, the Remote Work Agreement, and all related Company policies.
  • Maintain a safe, secure, and suitable Remote Workspace.
  • Be available during Core Hours and deliver agreed work.
  • Protect Company Equipment and Confidential Information.
  • Report incidents, injuries, and equipment problems promptly.
Manager
  • Assess requests fairly and consistently against role requirements.
  • Set clear goals and expectations, and hold regular check-ins.
  • Monitor performance by results and address concerns early.
  • Ensure team members complete required training and agreements.
  • Escalate policy breaches and incidents to HR or IT Security.
Human Resources
  • Maintain this policy and approve Remote Work Agreements.
  • Advise on eligibility, accommodations, and cross-border or legal issues.
  • Keep records of agreements and investigate breaches of this policy.
IT / Information Security
  • Provision, configure, and support Company Equipment and remote access.
  • Define and enforce security standards, including encryption and MFA.
  • Monitor for threats and respond to reported security incidents.
Finance
  • Process approved expense reimbursements and allowances.
  • Advise on tax and payroll implications of remote work arrangements.
Health & Safety Officer
  • Provide workspace and ergonomic guidance and self-assessment tools.
  • Record and investigate work-related incidents reported by remote employees.

9. Policy Violations and Review

9.1 Failure to comply with this policy may result in withdrawal of remote work privileges and disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment, in accordance with Company disciplinary procedures and applicable law.

9.2 Employees who have questions about this policy, or who wish to request an exception, should contact their Manager or HR. Exceptions must be approved in writing by HR.

9.3 This policy will be reviewed at least annually, and the Company may amend it at any time. Employees will be notified of material changes.

9.4 In the event of a conflict between this policy and applicable law or a collective agreement, the law or agreement will prevail.
